subject: MSA + Order Form: clarifying uptime measurement, maintenance triggers, and credit caps
messages:
From: Matthew Taylor <matthew.taylor@stratos.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 10, 2027 at 9:15 AM -0800
Subject: Redlines: MSA + Order Form (SLA section)

Hi Rachel / Redwood team,

Attached are our redlines for the MSA and the Order Form. Primary areas we changed: uptime targets, service credit formula, and a more prescriptive definition of planned maintenance (including advance notice and blackout windows).

Key asks from our side:
- We want 99.99% measured monthly for production endpoints.
- Service credits tiered and uncapped if downtime exceeds 1% in a month.
- 24/7 P1 response within 30 minutes and P2 within 4 hours.
- Planned maintenance limited to weekends UTC with >=72 hours notice; no more than 6 hours per maintenance event.

Please confirm which items you can accept and where you'd like to propose alternatives.

Attachments: redlined_MSA_20270210.pdf (pdf), redlined_OrderForm_20270210.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Matthew
Matthew Taylor
Sr. Counsel, Stratos Analytics
contracts@stratos.io

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Taylor <matthew.taylor@stratos.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 10, 2027 at 11:02 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form (SLA section)

Hi Matthew — thanks for sending these over and for being explicit about the asks. Well run a coordinated review between legal, product, and SRE. A few quick clarifying questions to make sure our counter is targeted: 

1) Uptime definition: are you measuring availability as successful 200 responses on the public inference endpoint, or do you want a more client-centric measurement (per-customer API key)?
2) Credits cap: when you say "uncapped" if >1% downtime, do you mean no cap on monthly credit percentage of monthly fees, or youre OK with a cap but tied to multiple thresholds?
3) Maintenance windows: do you have any regional blackout constraints (APAC mornings, EU evenings) we should be aware of?

Internally Ive attached a short SLA summary table to help compare our typical operational targets vs. yours. Were typically proposing 99.95% (monthly) for hosted tiers with a capped credit schedule — but we can propose a path to higher availability combined with a higher support commitment (SLA+).

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood legal (Jonas) to propose redline language for the SLA measurement and maintenance definition by EOD Thursday.
- Neha to draft an ops addendum describing on-call coverage and monitored escalation paths for P1/P2.
- Quick call Thursday 10:00 AM PT to walk the redlines if that works for your team.

Attachments: sla_summary_table.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Matthew Taylor <matthew.taylor@stratos.io>
Date: Thu, Feb 11, 2027 at 8:30 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form (SLA section)

Rachel / team — looping in my proposed language below. I kept things tight and operational so we avoid open-ended liabilities. Inline summary first, full clause draft below.

Summary of proposed positions:
- Measurement: availability measured at the per-tenant API endpoint over a rolling 30-day window; successful response defined as ingress request that returns a 2xx within configured timeout.
- Uptime target: 99.95% monthly (we can include an exception that for customers with a reserved Dedicated cluster and paid SLA+ we will consider 99.99% with a commensurate premium).
- Credits: tiered credits up to 50% of monthly fees per month for extreme outages; explicit cap of 200% of monthly fees in any single calendar month. No uncapped exposure.
- Response times: P1 initial response within 60 minutes (we can offer 30 minutes for SLA+ customers), P2 within 4 hours.
- Planned maintenance: defined windows (per-region): standard maintenance may occur between 00:00-06:00 UTC; we will provide >=72 hours notice; emergency maintenance permitted with as much notice as feasible. Individual maintenance events capped at 8 hours for high-impact changes.

Draft clause (copy into Order Form / schedule):

"Service Availability and Maintenance. Service Availability for the Hosted API shall be measured on a per-customer basis over each thirty (30) day billing period. Availability is calculated as the percentage of successful requests that receive an HTTP 2xx status within the configured request timeout, excluding (a) scheduled maintenance windows notified as set forth herein; (b) factors outside Redwood's reasonable control (force majeure); and (c) Customer-caused issues. Redwood targets 99.95% availability for standard Hosted plans. Customers may opt into a premium SLA (SLA+) supporting 99.99% availability subject to explicit order form commitment and fee adjustment.

Service Credits. If Redwood fails to meet the Availability target in any billing period, Customer may be eligible for service credits in accordance with the schedule attached to this Order Form. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for availability failures, and in no event shall Redwood's aggregate liability for availability failures exceed two (2) times Customer's fees for the affected month.

Planned Maintenance. Planned maintenance will be scheduled in regional windows (e.g., 00:00-06:00 UTC) with at least seventy-two (72) hours advance notice. Individual planned maintenance events for the Hosted API will not exceed eight (8) hours except in cases where additional time is required and agreed in advance.

Response Times and Escalation. Redwood will provide initial acknowledgement for Severity 1 incidents within sixty (60) minutes during the applicable coverage hours for standard customers; expedited acknowledgement and a 30-minute target may be provided for customers in the SLA+ program. Severity levels and escalation paths are defined in the attached Operations Addendum." 

I also linked our internal SLO playbook for the engineering folks: https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/0AExampleInternalSLOs

If you want, I can insert the exact credit percentage tiers into the Order Form draft and run through a final readout in the Thursday call.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Matthew Taylor <matthew.taylor@stratos.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 11, 2027 at 12:45 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form (SLA section)

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the clear draft. A couple follow-ups from our procurement and finance teams before we lock anything: 

- Can you confirm the monthly credit cap language exactly ("two (2) times Customer's fees for the affected month") — procurement prefers a hard cap but finance wants to avoid open-ended exposure; your formulation looks acceptable but well run it by CFO.
- On the measurement: wed like an option in the Order Form to select global vs per-tenant measurement. Some of our workloads are multi-tenant and our legal team prefers global measurement in a single-tenant contract; would you accept a clause that allows the Order Form to specify the measurement granularity?
- Response times: the 60-minute P1 acknowledgement is acceptable if the credit schedule reflects severity of impact. Can you add a short table that maps example impact scenarios to credit tiers?

I attached a short summary of our counters for quick reference: counter_redline_summary.pdf (pdf).

We can take the Thursday 10:00 AM PT call to finalize wording once we have your small edits.

Best regards,
Matthew Taylor
Sr. Counsel, Stratos Analytics
contracts@stratos.io
